introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, Advanced Level, 0710 Biology 1, June 2022. Multiple choice question paper. Time allowed: one and a half hours. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate and mark only one answer for each question on the answer sheet: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; do all rough work in the booklet.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Multiple choice questions** - choose the best answer, A, B, C or D.

**Directions for questions 21 to 28:** one or more of the responses (i) to (iv) is/are correct. Choose: **A** if (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; **B** if (i) and (iii) are correct; **C** if (ii) and (iv) are correct; **D** if only (iv) is correct.

**Directions for questions 42 to 50:** there are two statements. Read through the statements and then choose: **A** if both statements are true and the second explains the first; **B** if both statements are true but the second does not explain the first; **C** if the first statement is true and the second is false; **D** if the first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the organelle from which DNA is absent.
questions.corrige_markdown: DNA is found in the nucleus (linear chromosomes), and also in mitochondria and chloroplasts, which each contain a small circular DNA molecule inherited from their prokaryote-like ancestors. A ribosome is made only of ribosomal RNA and protein; it contains no DNA, since it is a site of translation, not a store of genetic information. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A newly transcribed mRNA molecule is usually longer than the sections of the gene that actually code for the protein. The actual codes in a eukaryotic gene are known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a eukaryotic gene the coding sequences are the **exons** (expressed regions). The primary transcript also contains **introns**, non-coding sequences that are cut out by splicing so that the mature mRNA is shorter than the primary transcript and contains only exons. Punctuation codons (start and stop) are triplets within the coding region, and nonsense codons are stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA); neither is the name for the coding sections of a gene. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The presence of a perivisceral cavity in the mesoderm of triploblastic multicellular organisms makes them to be called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **coelom** (perivisceral cavity) is a fluid-filled body cavity that is entirely lined by mesoderm; animals that have one are **coelomates** (annelids, molluscs, arthropods, vertebrates). Acoelomates (flatworms) have no body cavity, pseudocoelomates (roundworms) have a cavity that is only partly lined by mesoderm, and coelenterates (cnidarians) are diploblastic, with only two germ layers. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these passive mechanisms is responsible for the movement of substances across the cell surface membrane?
questions.corrige_markdown: A passive process needs no metabolic energy (ATP) because substances move down a concentration or electrochemical gradient: **diffusion** (including facilitated diffusion) is the passive mechanism here. Endocytosis and exocytosis are bulk-transport processes that need ATP, and active transport moves substances against their gradient using ATP and carrier proteins. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of relationship between living organisms of different species in which both partners benefit is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Mutualism** is an association between two species in which both gain (for example *Rhizobium* in the root nodules of legumes, which receive sugars while fixing nitrogen for the plant). In predation and parasitism one organism gains and the other is harmed, and in commensalism one gains while the other is neither helped nor harmed. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Algal blooms that occur in a fresh water lake is caused by ______ and leads to ______:
questions.corrige_markdown: An algal bloom is a sudden, massive growth of algae in water enriched with nitrates and phosphates, typically from the **discharge of sewage** (and fertiliser run-off). The enrichment is called **eutrophication**: the dense surface algae cut off light, the submerged plants die, and decomposition of the dead material by aerobic bacteria depletes oxygen so fish die. A, B and D do not name a source of nutrients: accumulation of soil, dead material or sand is not the cause of a bloom, and a bloom does not make navigation difficult as its main effect. Option C is the only one that gives a nutrient source, although its second part ('limiting primary productivity') is loosely worded. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: caused by an accumulation of soil in lakes; leads to a rise in temperature.
caused by an accumulation of dead material; leads to an increase in decomposition.
caused by discharge of sewage; leads to eutrophication limiting primary productivity.
caused by an accumulation of sand; leads to eutrophication which makes navigation difficult.

questions.enonce_markdown: Expiration in humans is usually stimulated by:
questions.corrige_markdown: The breathing centre in the medulla oblongata has an **inspiratory centre** in its dorsal (and lateral) part and an **expiratory centre** in its ventral (lower) part. Impulses carried by the phrenic nerve (diaphragm) and the external intercostal nerves (external intercostal muscles) cause inspiration, so options C and D are inspiratory. Quiet expiration is mostly passive (elastic recoil of the lungs); the expiratory centre is the part of the centre that stimulates expiration, and it drives the internal intercostal and abdominal muscles in forced expiration. The textbook answer is therefore the ventral or lower portion of the breathing centre. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the ventral or lower portion of the breathing center.

questions.enonce_markdown: If the water potential of a root hair cell is $-2000$ kPa and the pressure potential is $400$ kPa, the solute potential of the cell would be:
questions.corrige_markdown: Water potential is the sum of the solute potential and the pressure potential: $\psi_w = \psi_s + \psi_p$. So $\psi_s = \psi_w - \psi_p = -2000 - 400 = -2400$ kPa. The solute potential is always negative and is more negative than the water potential when the cell is turgid (positive pressure potential). Adding instead of subtracting gives the wrong value $-1600$ kPa. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In $C_3$ plants such as groundnut:
questions.corrige_markdown: In $C_3$ plants carbon dioxide is fixed in the stroma by ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase (RuBisCO), which joins $\mathrm{CO_2}$ to the acceptor ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP, a 5-carbon sugar); the first stable product is glycerate 3-phosphate (a 3-carbon compound). PEP is the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ acceptor and oxaloacetate the first product in $C_4$ plants such as maize; triose phosphate is formed later, when glycerate 3-phosphate is reduced using ATP and NADPH, so it is not the initial product. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the first product of photosynthesis is oxaloacetate.
the CO2 fixing enzyme is RUBP carboxylase.
the initial product of photosynthesis is triose phosphate.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the genotype of the offspring from a marriage between an albino man and a carrier woman?
questions.corrige_markdown: Albinism is recessive. Let A = normal allele, a = albinism allele. The albino man is $aa$ and the carrier woman is $Aa$. Gametes: man $a$; woman $A$ or $a$. Offspring: $\tfrac12\,Aa$ (carriers, normal phenotype) and $\tfrac12\,aa$ (albino). So half the children are carriers and half are albino. A carrier is not of 'normal genotype' (that would be $AA$), so option C is wrong, and A and B are impossible because the father can only give $a$. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: All the offspring obtained will have a normal genotype.
All the offspring produced will have the carrier genotype.
Half of the offspring produced will have the carrier genotype while the other half will have normal genotype.
Half of the offspring produced will have carrier genotype while the other half will have the albino genotype.

questions.enonce_markdown: Epithelial tissues arise from:
questions.corrige_markdown: The three embryonic germ layers all contribute epithelia: the epidermis and the lining of the mouth and anus come from the **ectoderm**; the lining of the gut and respiratory tract comes from the **endoderm**; and the lining of blood vessels (endothelium), kidney tubules and body cavities (mesothelium) comes from the **mesoderm**. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Darwin's statement 'survival of the fittest', means that:
questions.corrige_markdown: 'Fitness' in the Darwinian sense is the ability to survive and reproduce in a given environment: individuals whose variations make them best adapted to environmental change survive, breed and pass on those characters. It does not mean the largest, the most intelligent or the physically strongest. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the species most adaptable to changes survives.
the largest of the specie survives.
the most intelligent of the species survives.
the strongest of all species survives.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these statements correctly compares blood plasma and tissue fluid in a healthy person?

*Options as printed:* A) Blood plasma contains protein but tissue fluid lacks it.   B) Both blood plasma and tissue fluid contain red blood cells.   C) Tissue fluid contains white blood cells whereas blood plasma does not.   D) Tissue fluid is formed from blood plasma and is not returned to blood plasma.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tissue fluid is formed by pressure filtration of plasma through the capillary walls. Plasma proteins (albumin, globulins, fibrinogen) are too large to leave and tissue fluid therefore contains little or no protein, while plasma contains a high concentration: this is the standard textbook comparison and the most likely intended answer, option A (but 'lacks it' is stronger than the truth, because a trace of protein does leak out). Option B is false (red cells stay in the capillaries), option D is false (most tissue fluid returns to the capillaries at the venous end, the rest drains into the lymph). Option C is also defensible: plasma, the liquid part of blood, contains no cells, whereas phagocytic white blood cells squeeze out of capillaries and are present in tissue fluid.

**Intended answer: A (Blood plasma contains protein but tissue fluid lacks it).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the nucleoside amongst the following:
questions.corrige_markdown: A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base joined to a pentose sugar with no phosphate group: adenosine is adenine + ribose. Adenosine monophosphate (AMP) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) are nucleotides (nucleoside + one or three phosphates), and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) is a dinucleotide. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which driving force moves mineral salts in the xylem vessel of a plant?
questions.corrige_markdown: Mineral ions are carried in the water of the xylem, which is moved by transpiration pull (cohesion-tension) in the day and by **root pressure**, generated when the endodermis actively secretes ions into the xylem so that water follows by osmosis and pushes the sap upward. Among the options given only root pressure is a force acting on the sap in the xylem: osmosis is the movement of water (not salts) across membranes, translocation is transport of organic solutes in the phloem, and active transport is a membrane process that needs living cells, whereas xylem vessels are dead and empty. The better answer, transpiration pull, is not among the options. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Deduce the number of chromosomes in the microspore mother cells of maize plant having 20 chromosomes in the cells of the leaf.
questions.corrige_markdown: Leaf cells are somatic and diploid, so $2n = 20$ (haploid number $n = 10$). A microspore mother cell (pollen mother cell) in the anther is also a diploid cell of the sporophyte, so it has **20** chromosomes. It divides by meiosis to give four haploid microspores (pollen grains), each with 10 chromosomes; 10 is therefore the number in the microspores, not in the mother cells. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A type of classification which avoids the problem of establishing evolutionary relationships is:

*Options as printed:* A) Artificial classification.   B) Phenetic classification.   C) Numerical classification.   D) Phylogenetic classification.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Phenetic classification groups organisms by overall observable similarity (as many characters as possible, weighted equally, often analysed numerically) and makes no attempt to infer common ancestry, so it avoids the problem of establishing evolutionary relationships. Phylogenetic classification is the one that tries to reflect evolutionary relationships. However the printed options are not exclusive: artificial classification (a few convenient features) and numerical classification (the numerical methods of phenetics) also ignore evolutionary relationships, so the printed key cannot be fixed with certainty; the most likely intended answer is B.

**Intended answer: B (Phenetic classification).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The speed of transmission of a nerve impulse is increased in a vertebrate neuron by:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a myelinated axon the myelin sheath insulates the membrane, so action potentials jump from node of Ranvier to node (saltatory conduction), which is much faster than continuous conduction along an unmyelinated axon. A low temperature slows the diffusion of ions and enzyme activity so it slows conduction, a smaller axon diameter increases resistance and slows conduction, and stimulus intensity changes the frequency of impulses, not their speed (all-or-nothing law). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: a low temperature of less than 20 degrees C.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these is the best description of a transgenic organism?

*Options as printed:* A) New genes that have been inserted into the embryos of plants and animals.   B) New genes that have been inserted into plant embryos.   C) New genes that have been inserted into animal embryos.   D) Organisms containing new genes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A transgenic organism is an organism whose genome contains a gene (transgene) from another organism that has been introduced by genetic engineering. Options A, B and C describe the new genes (and only where they were inserted), not an organism, and they restrict the case to embryos; only option D actually describes an organism, so D is the most likely intended answer. The printed question is loosely worded, however (A could also be defended as the description of how transgenic plants and animals are made), so it is not safe to mark automatically.

**Intended answer: D (Organisms containing new genes).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The growth pattern observed in mammals e.g. man is known as:

*Options as printed:* A) Limited growth.   B) Isometric growth.   C) Allometric growth.   D) Unlimited growth.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mammals show **limited growth**: growth is rapid early in life and stops once the adult size is reached (the growth curve is S-shaped and levels off). Unlimited growth is typical of plants, which keep growing throughout life; isometric growth means all parts grow at the same rate (fish, some insects). The printed question is ambiguous because man is also the usual example of allometric growth (head, trunk and limbs grow at different rates), so the key cannot be fixed with certainty; the most likely intended answer is A.

**Intended answer: A (Limited growth).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The frequency of the dominant and recessive allele in a population will remain constant if:

- (i) the population is small.
- (ii) there is random mating.
- (iii) some genotypes are not fertile.
- (iv) no mutation occurs.
questions.corrige_markdown: These are conditions of the Hardy-Weinberg principle. (i) is false: the population must be large, because in a small population chance (genetic drift) changes allele frequencies. (ii) is true: mating must be random. (iii) is false: all genotypes must be equally fertile and viable, otherwise selection changes the frequencies. (iv) is true: mutations alter allele frequencies. The true statements are (ii) and (iv). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The transmission of impulses across a synapse gives the following advantages to the body:

- (i) enables information from different parts of the nervous system to be identified.
- (ii) provides a mechanism for filtering out trivial or non-essential information.
- (iii) slows down transmission leading to short reaction time.
- (iv) ensures that nerve impulses are in a one-way motion.
questions.corrige_markdown: (ii) is true: a postsynaptic neuron fires only when enough neurotransmitter has accumulated (summation to reach threshold), so weak background impulses are filtered out. (iv) is true: neurotransmitter is released only by the presynaptic membrane and receptors are only on the postsynaptic membrane, so transmission is one-way. (iii) is false: the synaptic delay (about 0.5 ms) slows transmission and therefore lengthens, not shortens, the reaction time, so the statement contradicts itself. Statement (i) is worded 'identified' (integration of information from many neurones is the usual advantage), so it is doubtful as printed. Only option C avoids statement (iii), and A and B include it. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these processes occur by mitosis?

- (i) Cloning of plasma cells.
- (ii) Gamete production.
- (iii) Replacing damaged cells.
- (iv) Formation of spores in the moss plant.
questions.corrige_markdown: (i) is true: after antigen selection a B lymphocyte divides by mitosis into a clone of plasma cells and memory cells. (iii) is true: tissue repair and replacement are by mitosis. (ii) is false in the usual sense: gametes of animals and flowering plants are produced by meiosis (the moss gametophyte, already haploid, forms its gametes by mitosis, but the statement is taken in general). (iv) is false: spores of a moss are formed by meiosis in the capsule of the sporophyte. The true statements are (i) and (iii). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the description which best defines the Xiphoid cartilage.

- (i) Serves as an attachment point for organs and large muscles of the diaphragm.
- (ii) Indicates where chest compressions may be ministered.
- (iii) Is the smallest region of the sternum also called metasternum.
- (iv) Develops into bone at adulthood especially in guinea pigs.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct   B) (i) and (iii) are correct   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct   D) only (iv) is correct
questions.corrige_markdown:
The xiphoid process (xiphoid cartilage) is the small, lowest part of the sternum, also called the metasternum: (iii) is true. It is cartilage in the young and ossifies in adults, so (iv) is true for humans, although 'especially in guinea pigs' is not a standard statement. It gives attachment to the diaphragm and to the rectus abdominis, so (i) is roughly true (but muscles, not 'organs'), and in first aid it is a landmark used to place the hands for chest compressions on the lower half of the sternum, so (ii) is a practical rather than a defining statement. With these readings the true set could be (iii) and (iv), or (i), (ii) and (iii), or others, and none of the printed combinations can be shown to be the unique correct one. The question is therefore left open for self-assessment.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following occurs when the eye is exposed to bright light?

- (i) The circular muscles of the iris contract reducing the pupil size.
- (ii) The radial muscles contract increasing the pupil size.
- (iii) The radial muscles contract increasing the pupil size.
- (iv) Much light enters the eye.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct   B) (i) and (iii) are correct   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct   D) only (iv) is correct
questions.corrige_markdown:
In bright light the pupil constricts (pupil reflex): the circular (sphincter) muscles of the iris contract and the radial (dilator) muscles relax, so less light enters the eye and the retina is protected. Statement (i) is true. Statements (ii) and (iii) are identical as printed and false: contraction of the radial muscles dilates the pupil, which happens in dim light. Statement (iv) is true as a description of the stimulus. The correct pair, (i) and (iv), is not offered (B is (i) and (iii), and (iii) repeats the false statement (ii)), so the printed question is defective and cannot be marked automatically.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sympatric speciation may occur when:

- (i) there is fusion of gametes.
- (ii) the gametes are prevented from meeting.
- (iii) the genitalia of two groups are compatible.
- (iv) the development of the embryo is impossible.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sympatric speciation is the formation of new species in the same area through reproductive isolation. (ii) is true (gametic isolation: the gametes of the two groups do not meet or fuse). (iv) is true (post-zygotic isolation: the hybrid embryo cannot develop). (i) is false: fusion of gametes between the groups would keep them one gene pool. (iii) is false: compatible genitalia allow mating, so they do not isolate; it is incompatible genitalia (mechanical isolation) that would. The true statements are (ii) and (iv). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the relationship that can best define interspecific competition.

- (i) Toads, birds, humans and weaver birds catching termites.
- (ii) Human beings from different villages competing for land.
- (iii) Pear trees, eucalyptus trees, coffee plants and kola nut trees competing for mineral salts in the soil.
- (iv) Guinea pigs scrambling over banana leaves that have been introduced in to a room.
questions.corrige_markdown: Interspecific competition is competition between individuals of **different species** for the same limited resource. (i) is true: toads, birds, humans and weaver birds are different species competing for termites (food). (iii) is true: four different plant species compete for mineral salts. (ii) is false: human beings from different villages are one species (intraspecific competition). (iv) is false: guinea pigs are one species (intraspecific competition). The true statements are (i) and (iii). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Choose the statement(s) that is/are applicable to both onion epidermis and human red blood cells.

- (i) Have a nucleus.
- (ii) Possess a cell membrane.
- (iii) Chloroplast absent.
- (iv) Presence of pyrenoids.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct   B) (i) and (iii) are correct   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct   D) only (iv) is correct
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) is false for the pair: onion epidermal cells have a nucleus but mature human red blood cells have lost theirs. (ii) is true: all cells have a cell surface membrane. (iii) is true: onion epidermis (a non-photosynthetic tissue of a storage bulb) has no chloroplasts, and neither do red blood cells. (iv) is false: pyrenoids are found in the chloroplasts of algae and some other plants such as hornworts, not in onion epidermis or red blood cells. The correct pair, (ii) and (iii), is not among the printed combinations (A includes (i), B includes (i), C includes (iv)), so the printed question is defective and cannot be marked automatically.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: At which stage of development is the egg ready for ovulation?
questions.corrige_markdown: At ovulation the mature (Graafian) follicle ruptures and releases a **secondary oocyte**, arrested at metaphase of meiosis II; it completes meiosis II only if a sperm penetrates it. The oogonium is the diploid germ cell that divides by mitosis before birth, the primary oocyte is arrested in prophase I inside the primary follicle, and a primary follicle is a stage of the follicle (an oocyte surrounded by follicle cells), not the egg itself. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The juxtaglomerular complex which is under control of the sympathetic nervous system is responsible for the secretion of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The juxtaglomerular apparatus lies where the distal convoluted tubule touches the afferent arteriole. Its granular cells secrete **renin** when blood pressure or blood sodium falls, and also when stimulated by sympathetic nerves. Renin converts angiotensinogen (made in the liver) to angiotensin I, leading to angiotensin II and then aldosterone (secreted by the adrenal cortex); progesterone is an ovarian hormone. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The synthesis of ATP in a cell requires one of the following:
questions.corrige_markdown: ATP is a nucleotide made of the base adenine, the pentose sugar **ribose** and three phosphate groups, so ribose is needed to synthesise it (together with adenine and phosphate, from ADP + $\mathrm{P_i}$). Deoxyribose is the sugar of DNA nucleotides, a hexose sugar is respired to release energy and is not a part of ATP, and ribulose bisphosphate is the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ acceptor of the Calvin cycle. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The light independent stage of photosynthesis is sometimes referred to as a "dark" reaction because:
questions.corrige_markdown: The Calvin cycle (stroma of the chloroplast) does not need light directly: it uses ATP and reduced NADP made by the light-dependent stage, and so it is called the 'dark' reaction. This is the meaning of option B ('it does not require light' directly). Option A is true but is a reason for its dependence on the light stage, not for the name; option C is the opposite of the idea (it can go on in the light but is not named because of it); and option D is false because the stage occurs by day, when ATP and NADPH are supplied (it is not restricted to the night). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: it requires the product of the light stage.
it occurs simultaneously with the light stage in the chloroplast.
it occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast only at night.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the correct order of the sequence of electrical impulses passing through the cardiac muscles of the heart during contraction.
questions.corrige_markdown: Each heartbeat begins in the **sinoatrial node** (pacemaker, wall of the right atrium). The wave spreads over the right and left atria (atrial systole), reaches the **atrioventricular node**, where it is delayed about 0.1 s, then passes down the bundle of His and **Purkinje tissue** (fibres) in the septum to the ventricular walls. The sequence SAN, atria, AVN, Purkinje tissue is in option B. In options A and D the atria are stimulated before the sinoatrial node, and in C Purkinje tissue comes before the atrioventricular node. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Right and left atria -> sinoatrial node -> atrioventricular node -> ventricular walls.
Sinoatrial node -> right and left atria -> atrioventricular node -> Purkinje's tissue.
Sinoatrial node -> right and left atria -> Purkinje's tissue -> atrioventricular node.
Right and left atria -> sinoatrial node -> Purkinje's tissue -> ventricular walls.

questions.enonce_markdown: Where is the filtrate from the glomerulus deposited?
questions.corrige_markdown: Ultrafiltration forces water and small solutes out of the glomerular capillaries through the capillary wall, basement membrane and the podocytes of the **Bowman's capsule**; the glomerular filtrate is collected in the space of the capsule and then flows into the proximal convoluted tubule. The loop of Henle and the distal tubule are later parts of the nephron. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the reagents used, and the color of the end product obtained for a positive test for reducing sugars.
questions.corrige_markdown: The test for a reducing sugar uses Benedict's solution or Fehling's solution (Fehling's A, copper(II) sulphate, and Fehling's B, sodium hydroxide and sodium potassium tartrate, mixed in equal volumes) and **heating** in a water bath: the reducing sugar reduces blue $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ to copper(I) oxide, $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$, giving a **brick-red** precipitate (green, yellow and orange precipitates mean lower concentrations). Option A has the right reagents, heat and the maximum colour. Options B and D leave out the heating. Option C describes the biuret test of proteins (copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide, violet or purple) and does not need heat. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Fehling's A and B + test solution + heat; brick red.
CuSO4 + NaOH + test solution + heat; Purple.
Fehling's A and B + test solution; brick red.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the most suitable medium for breeding *Drosophila melanogaster*?
questions.corrige_markdown: *Drosophila* (the fruit fly) feeds on and lays its eggs in yeast growing on fermenting fruit. In practice (in Cameroon, as in textbooks) the culture medium is ripe fruit such as banana or pineapple peelings, which supply sugar and yeast and are cheap. Agar is only a setting agent that has to be enriched with sugar, maize meal and yeast; moist bread and cow dung do not give a stable yeast-rich food. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Chlorosis in older leaves of plant is a deficiency disease due to the lack of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorosis is the yellowing of leaves caused by a failure to make chlorophyll. When the deficient element is **mobile** in the plant, it is withdrawn from the older leaves to the young growing ones, so older leaves become chlorotic first. Nitrogen (needed for chlorophyll and proteins) is mobile, so its deficiency shows in older leaves. Calcium and manganese are poorly mobile (their deficiency shows in young leaves), and sodium is not an essential element for most plants. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The characteristics that proves that frogs have evolved from fishes is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The **tadpole larva** is aquatic, breathes with gills, has a lateral line, a tail and a two-chambered heart like a fish: it shows the fish-like (aquatic) ancestry of amphibians, which is retained in the larval stage. Swimming in water, feeding on aquatic plants and a similar head shape are not evidence of common ancestry. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: their ability to swim in water.
similarity in the shape of the head.

questions.enonce_markdown: What structure separates the outer and middle ear?
questions.corrige_markdown: The **tympanic membrane** (eardrum) closes the inner end of the external auditory canal and separates the outer ear from the middle ear; it vibrates with sound waves and passes them to the ear ossicles. The pinna belongs to the outer ear, the oval window separates the middle ear from the inner ear, and the cochlea is in the inner ear. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The amount of air that can be inhaled or exhaled during one respiratory cycle is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The **tidal volume** is the volume of air breathed in or out in one ordinary breath (about 500 cm$^3$ in an adult at rest). The residual volume is the air that stays in the lungs after the most forceful expiration, the lung (vital) capacity is the largest volume that can be exhaled after a maximum inhalation, and the reserve volumes are the extra air that can be breathed in or out by force. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The correct sequence for urine formation in the kidney is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Urine is formed in three stages along the nephron: first **ultrafiltration** in the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, then **selective reabsorption** (mainly in the proximal tubule, with water and salts later) and finally **secretion** of substances such as H$^+$, K$^+$ and drugs into the tubule. The correct order is filtration, reabsorption, secretion. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Antigens are cell identity markers that stimulate the production of specific antibodies.

**Second statement:** Artificial passive immunity is obtained by a foetus obtaining antibodies through the placenta.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: antigens are molecules (usually proteins or glycoproteins) on the surface of cells that identify them as self or non-self and that stimulate B lymphocytes to make specific antibodies. The second statement is false: antibodies that cross the placenta give **natural** passive immunity; artificial passive immunity is obtained by injecting ready-made antibodies (an antiserum, for example against tetanus or snake venom). The first is true and the second is false. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** When temperature falls in man, the best way to trigger the natural homeostatic mechanism to bring it to norm is to take in hot coffee.

**Second statement:** High temperature in man resulting from the release of merozoites by schizogony is treated by bathing with very cold water.

*Options as printed:* A) Both statements are true and the second explains the first   B) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first   C) The first statement is true and the second is false   D) The first statement is false and the second is true
questions.corrige_markdown:
The first statement is not correct: the natural homeostatic response to a fall in body temperature (detected by the hypothalamus) is shivering, vasoconstriction of skin arterioles, erection of hairs and a raised metabolic rate; hot coffee is an external source of heat and does not trigger these mechanisms. The second statement is not correct either: the fever of malaria (merozoites released from red cells by schizogony) is lowered by tepid sponging and treated with antimalarial drugs; very cold water causes vasoconstriction and shivering, which hold heat in and are harmful. Both statements are false, and the printed options do not contain 'both false', so no printed option fits and the question is left open for self-assessment.



The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The epiphysis of a typical long bone like the femur contains trabeculae.

**Second statement:** Osteocytes arise from chondroblast and possess canaliculi.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: the epiphysis is made of spongy (cancellous) bone, a network of bony struts called trabeculae with red marrow between them. The second statement is false: osteocytes are mature bone cells that arise from **osteoblasts** (bone-forming cells), not from chondroblasts, which form cartilage; it is true that osteocytes lie in lacunae and send out processes through canaliculi. First true, second false. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** In recombinant DNA technology, human genes are often transferred into bacteria (prokaryotes) or yeast (eukaryote).

**Second statement:** Both bacteria and yeast multiply very fast to form huge populations, which express the desired gene.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: bacteria (such as *E. coli*) and yeast are the usual host cells for human genes, for example the genes for insulin and growth hormone. The second statement is also true, and it gives the reason why these hosts are chosen: they divide quickly (a bacterium every 20 minutes or so), so a single transformed cell gives a huge clone of cells that all express the gene and make the human protein cheaply. The second explains the first. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Synergism occurs in plants when the combined action of two growth factors produces a greater effect.

**Second statement:** Auxins (IAA) and cytokinins promote mitotic cell division at the meristems.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: in synergism the combined effect of two hormones is greater than the sum of their separate effects. The second statement is also true: auxin and cytokinin together stimulate mitosis and cytokinesis in meristems (and in tissue culture). It is an example of synergism, but it does not explain what synergism is or why it happens, so the second does not explain the first (the printed pair could be read either way, but the second is an illustration, not a cause). Both true, second does not explain first. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Diseases like Measles and Tuberculosis only attack people once.

**Second statement:** A previous infection induces the primary immune response to produce specific memory cells making the individual immune to future infections.
questions.corrige_markdown: The second statement is true: a first infection causes the primary immune response, in which B and T lymphocytes divide and form memory cells that respond quickly and strongly to the same antigen later (secondary response), so the person is immune. It explains the statement that diseases such as measles, with a stable antigen, attack a person only once. The first statement is accepted as true in the usual textbook treatment, although tuberculosis can recur in some people and is not as strictly 'once only' as measles. Both true, and the second explains the first. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Asexual reproduction is a very fast process and produces offspring that are identical to the parents.

**Second statement:** Asexual reproduction is more common in animals than in plants and that is why there are more animals on earth than plants.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: asexual reproduction involves one parent and mitosis only, it is fast, and the offspring are genetically identical clones of the parent. The second statement is false: asexual reproduction (vegetative propagation, budding, fission) is more common in plants, fungi and bacteria than in animals, and plants (including all the algae and the forests) far outnumber animals in biomass. First true, second false. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Hemolytic disease of the new born (HDN) is a blood disorder which occurs as a result of incompatibility between the blood types of a mother and her baby.

**Second statement:** HDN most frequently occurs when rhesus negative mother has a baby with rhesus positive father.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: HDN (erythroblastosis fetalis) happens when the mother's antibodies destroy the baby's red blood cells. The second statement is true and states the commonest incompatibility: a rhesus negative mother carrying a rhesus positive baby (the baby inherits the Rh+ allele from the Rh+ father). At the first birth fetal Rh+ cells enter the mother's blood and she makes anti-D antibodies, which in a later pregnancy cross the placenta and haemolyse the red cells of an Rh+ fetus. The second gives the particular incompatibility that causes the disorder, so it explains the first. (The printed second statement says 'baby with a rhesus positive father'; it is the baby's Rh+ blood group that matters.) **Answer: A.**
